this course provides a complete and straightforward coverage of the basics of electrical component and circuits. fundamental circuit laws and analysis methods are discussed in a variety of basic circuits. major topics included are ohm’s law, kirchhoff’s laws, magnetism and electromagnetism, reactance, impedance, resonance, and passive filters

extracted_text: information systems and the strategies for managing them change quickly, but the concepts that guide both often remain timeless. these principles form the backbone of this comprehensive survey of the field, designed for a student’s first course in information systems. by presenting the details and the big picture, this course puts the lessons of managing information systems into an understandable context. the overall principle is that the right information, if it is delivered to the right person, in the right fashion, and at the right time, can improve and ensure organizational effectiveness and efficiency.

this course is aimed to give students knowledge and skills on how to generate data structure using java as well as to use ood to solve a particular problem. data structure consists of linked list, stacks, queues, binary trees, stack, queue and graph

upon completion of the course the student should be able to  understand the object oriented programming, inheritance, and class hierarchies including inter faces and abstract classes.. understand the java collections framework as the foundation for the traditional data structures.. understand the concept of stacks, queues, and deques understand the concept of recursive data structure. understand the concept of binary trees, including binary search trees, heaps, priority queues, and huffman trees understand the concept of set and map interfaces understand the concept of stack and queue. understand the concept of various sorting algorithms including mergesort, heapsort, quicksort and timsort. understand the concept of self balancing search trees, focusing on algorithms for manipulating them. included are avl and red black trees, 2 3 trees, 24 trees, b trees, and skip lists. understand the concept of graphs.
classroom instruction consists of lectures and practical problem solving, supplemented by visual aids designed to assist the student to successfully meet the course’s learning objectives.

extracted_text: the pancasila and citizenship education (ppkn) course is one of the courses that will lead students to strengthen their personality and be able to consistently apply pancasila values in everyday life so that they become citizens with strong national character and vision, polite and personal personality. moral, able to think critically and analytically, and able to be proactive in responding and being a solution to a number of challenges and problems faced by the indonesian nation in the future, especially at the global level. through this course, it is hoped that students can build a strong knowledge base regarding the important role of pancasila in the life of the state, the basics of citizenship (civic knowledge), citizenship skills (civic skills), citizenship attitudes (civic disposition) and citizenship ethics (civic ethics) in respect the diversity of indonesia, be democratic and maintain the building of national unity and integrity. by obtaining well structured materials and discussions, it is hoped that students will be able to strengthen students' understanding of the country's historical, juridical, and national territorial insights, as well as provide geopolitical and geostrategic insights in efforts to develop all fields in an effort to encourage indonesia's role and excellence in participating. and realizing world peace on the basis of independence.

this course presents a comprehensive overview of data communications. it is based on the bottom up approach to data communications. the course emphasizes data communications concepts as outlined by the 7 layer open system interconnection (osi). this course introduces the architecture, structure, func tions, components, and models of data communication network including computer network, internet, and mobile. the principles and structure of ip addressing and the fundamentals of ethernet concepts, media, and operations are introduced to provide a foundation for the curriculum.

noise and symbols. understand the different media available to support data communications. understand the role of the various protocols in facilitating the transfer of data across a communi cation network. appreciate the role of the iso seven layer model which attempts to standardise communication the above mentioned objectives should be aligned into the following competences a. knowledge the course is delivered as a class based course. classroom instruction consists of lectures and practical problem solving, supplemented by visual aids designed to assist the student to successfully meet the course’s learning objectives. it is imperative that students take an active interest in the course. to succeed in this course, students must read, think, and write in a critical and analytical manner and this takes time and practice. such practice can only be achieved by working theoretical and practical exercises. when troubles arise, and they will, the student must ask questions which may be directed to the instructor or other students in a variety of ways. students are also encouraged to work together on problem sets as part of their exercises. however, individual must ultimately demonstrate the understanding of the material by writing up his/her own solutions without the help of other students or their written work. on average students need to spend, at least, 6 hours of study and preparation per week for this course.

extracted_text: deskripsi matakuliah the leadership and management challenge is to design contexts (jobs, organizational cultures, structures, processes) that enable individuals and groups to thrive. the personal challenge is how to find and/or create a context in which student thrive and lead at their best in the future. the course maintains this dual focus (1) on student (next) role as leader and manager, designing and enabling contexts where others can thrive; but at the same time (2) on student personal quest to find and create contexts where you flourish and perform at your best. much of the course draws from a paradigm for managerial practice called positive organizational scholarship (pos), a newly domain in organizational study, as well as the basic management skills that required to be a good manager leader. the core premise of this paradigm is that leadership and personal excellence are fundamentally tied to creating/enabling organizational contexts that build human strengths as well as unlock the positive and generative dynamics of vibrant human communities as well as achieve the business goal.

extracted_text: this course introduces the architecture, structure, functions, components, and models of the internet and other computer networks. students achieve a basic understanding of how networks operate and how to build simple local area networks (lan), perform basic configurations for routers and switches, and implement internet protocol (ip). additionally, packet tracer (pt) activities reinforce new concepts, and allow students to model and analyze routing processes that may be difficult to visualize or understand.

source_file: Copy of FTK205 LAN and Wireless.pdf
extracted_text: this curriculum provides students with the skills needed to succeed in networking related degree pro grams and helps them prepare for ccna certification. it also helps students develop the skills necessary to fulfill the job responsibilities of network technicians, network administrators, and network engineers. it provides a theoretically rich, hands on introduction to networking and the internet. the goal of this course is to introduce the students fundamental networking concepts and technologies. the course will assist students in developing the skills necessary to plan and implement small network across a range of applications. by the end of the course, students will be able to build simple local area networks (lan), perform basic configurations for routers and switches, and implement ip addressing schemes. upon completion of this course, the student should be able to (cid 136) configure switches and end devices to provide access to local and remote network resources. (cid 136) explain how physical and data link layer protocols support the operation of ethernet in a switched network. (cid 136) configure routers to enable end to end connectivity between remote devices. (cid 136) create ipv4 and ipv6 addressing schemes and verify network connectivity between devices. (cid 136) explain how the upper layers of the osi model support network applications. (cid 136) configure a small network with security best practices. (cid 136) troubleshoot connectivity in a small network.

classroom instruction consists of lectures and practical problem solving, supplemented by visual aids designed to assist the student to successfully meet the courses learning objectives. it is imperative that students take an active interest in the course. to succeed in this course, students must read, think, and write in a critical and analytical manner and this takes time and practice. such practice can only be achieved by working exercises. when troubles arise, and they will, the student must ask questions which may be directed to the instructor or other students in a variety of ways. students are also encouraged to work individually and together with the class mates on problem sets as part of their exercises. however, individual must ultimately demonstrate the understanding of the substantial by writing up his/her own solutions. moreover, there will be a workshop/ discussion/ class assignment and presentation both in written and oral manner in order to evaluate the students level of knowledge and skills on this course. mid test is conducted in written essay tests to evaluate the students level of knowledge on this course. and, the final test is conducted by students in written essay tests or presentation. on average students need to spend, at least, 6 hours of study and preparation per week for this course. f ppkr1 syllabus tif210 tif41w (rencana pembelajaran semester)

deskripsi matakuliah interpersonal skill merupakan bagian dari soft skills dalam pengembangan karakter yang merupakan tuntutan dari perkembangan zaman seperti media sosial, pasar bebas, teknologi, informasi dan tantangan kebutuhan global. tuntutan dari perkembangan paham inklusi sosial, budaya, ekonomi dan perkembangan politik agar bijak dan cakap dalam membangun relasi sosial antar sesama manusia didalam pekerjaaan, komunitas dan hidup sehari hari, di masyarakat, di kantor, di media sosial, di jalan, di dalam organisasi, di dunia bisnis dan lain lain.

sasaran kompetensi lulusan yang dibebankan pada matakuliah mengaktualisasi diri secara baik, berani dan benar ( citra diri yang baik ). menjaga keharmonisan dalam hubungan pergaulan hidup sehari hari dimana saja dan kapan saja. mengkomunikasikan informasi yang benar, cepat dan tepat. membangun komunitas atau team yang solid, harmonis dan bersinergi secara baik dan optimal. menempatkan diri secara benar dan tepat pada bidangnya menjadi pemecah masalah bukan sumber masalah. menjadi pribadi yang menyenangkan dan yang bermanfaat bagi dunia dan kemuliaan tuhan menjadi negosiator, persuasitor dan pemimpin yang bijak, cakap dan berhasil

extracted_text: this course describes the architecture, components, and operations of routers and switches in a larger and more complex network. switching, routing, and wireless essentials (srwe) advances the student’s knowledge of the operation of routers and switches in small networks. srwe will introduce the student to wireless local area networks (wlans) and network security concepts. each chapter walks the student through basic configuration, implementation, and troubleshooting principles. additionally, packet tracer (pt) activities reinforce new concepts, and allow students to model and analyze routing processes that may be difficult to visualize or understand.

extracted_text: this course focuses on the wan technologies and network services required by converged ap plications in a complex network. describes different wan technologies and their benefits, the operations and benefits of virtual private network (vpn) and tunneling and also network ar chitectures. the students learn to configure, troubleshoot serial and broadband connections, extended acls operations. finally, the students learn how to detect, troubleshoot and correct common enterprise network implementation issues. each chapter walks the student through basic configuration, implementation, and troubleshooting principles. additionally, packet tracer (pt) activities reinforce new concepts, and allow students to model and analyze routing processes that may be difficult to visualize or understand.

extracted_text: this curriculum provides students with the skills needed to succeed in networking related degree programs and helps them prepare for ccna certification. it also helps students develop the skills necessary to fulfill the job responsibilities of network technicians, network administrators, and network engineers. it provides a theoretically rich, hands on introduction to networking and the internet. the goal of this course is to introduce the students fundamental networking concepts and technologies. the course will assist students in developing the skills necessary to plan and implement small network across a range of applications. upon completion of this course, the student should be able to  learn the fundamentals enterprise wans, the technologies available to implement them and the technical terminology. describe today’s increasing network security threats and explain the need to implement a comprehensive security policy to mitigate the threats. learn the serial point to point communications and the point to point protocol (ppp). learn the importance of security to find a balance between the need to open networks and the need to protect business information, and learn the security threats and mitigation techniques. learn how to securing site to site connectivity. learn the broadband technologies from telecommuter’s perspective, such as cable, dsl, wireless broadband and vpns. learn to identify teleworker requirements and it architectures, and introduction to ipv6. learn to monitor the network using network monitoring tools. learn how to establish a network baseline and learn to develop network documentation to help in network troubleshooting.

this course will cover the topic of distributed systems materials an introduction to distributed systems, architectures of distributed systems, processes, communications, naming, synchronization, consistency and replication, fault tolerance, security related to distributed systems, distributed object based, web based, coordination based systems, and distributed file systems.

the objectives of this course are as follows  present the principles underlying the function of distributed systems and their extension to grid computing, cloud computing and virtualization techniques. create an awareness of the fundamental technical challenges in distributed systems design and implementation. expose students to current technology used to build architecture to enhance distributed comput ing infrastructures with various computing principles and paradigms, including grid and cloud computing. enhance students’ understanding of key issues related to multi level interoperability across a dis tributed infrastructure and across multiple heterogeneous and distributed resources in a dynami cally changing computing environment. expose students to past and current research issues in the field of distributed systems and new challenges in cloud computing. provide experience in analyzing a distributed computing model and implementing typical algo rithms used in distributed systems and distributed applications in cloud infrastructure. explain what a distributed system is, why the student would design a system as a distributed system, and what the desired properties of such systems are. list the principles underlying the functioning of distributed systems, describe the problems and challenges associated with these principles and evaluate the effectiveness and shortcomings of their solutions. recognize how the principles are applied in contemporary distributed systems, explain how they affect the software design, and be able to identify features and design decisions that may cause problems. f ppkr1 syllabus tif309 (rencana pembelajaran semester) design a distributed system that fulfills requirements with regards to key distributed system prop erties (such as scalability, transparency, etc), be able to recognize when this is not possible and explain why. build distributed system software using both basic os mechanisms as well as higher level middle ware and languages.

this lecture will discuss an exploration of tools, techniques, issues and problems arising from the devel opment of computer networks, and the requirement to manage them. the module considers the range of network management tasks from initial planning through to the security and operational aspects of network usage. throughout, the emphasis is on the use of the methods considered, with each aspect of the system being placed in a realistic context.

upon completion of this course, the student should be able to (cid 136) describe the concept of behavior of a network system from the viewpoint of a user. (cid 136) discuss the operational requirements arising from the demands of users. (cid 136) evaluate the impact of a range of application types on a communications system. (cid 136) determine the effectiveness of various communications mechanisms and protocols in handling that impact. (cid 136) recognize the need for management in a networking environment, and understand how that need may be met. (cid 136) select suitable information collection methodologies to allow the behaviour of a network to be controlled. (cid 136) apply simulation techniques to the prediction of the behavior of a network.

course_name: Etika Profesi dan Hak Kekayaan Intelektual
extracted_text: deskripsi matakuliah ethics and information technology concerns the ethical dilemmas that exist where human beings, information objects, and social computing technologies interact. the course explores an emerging model of information ethics from historical and cross cultural perspectives and then applies this model to a variety of new and emerging technologies that are inherently social in their construction and use. examples of issues that the course covers in discrete modules that cover such topics as social media interaction; remembering and forgetting; and game design ethics. students explore the technological underpinnings of associated technology systems, experiment with individual and group interaction with technologies, and examine the mechanics of ethical and unethical behaviors.
